definitions.explanation: A traditional given name for a boy, once typical for an eldest son, and the stock name for a Japanese man in folk tales, textbooks and sample forms.

examples.japanese: {記入例|きにゅうれい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「{山田太郎|やまだたろう}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いてある→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: The sample filled-in form says "Yamada Taro".

examples.japanese: ⟦{長男|ちょうなん}→長男：14519_chounan⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{太郎|たろう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{名付|なづ}けられた→名付ける：11998_nazukeru⟧。
examples.english: He was named Taro because he was the eldest son.

examples.japanese: ⟦{桃太郎|ももたろう}→桃太郎：30946_momotarou⟧や{浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧、⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{太郎|たろう}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Many folk-tale heroes, such as Momotaro and Urashima Taro, have names ending in Taro.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{太|た} (big) + {郎|ろう} (son): traditionally the name of a first son, with {次郎|じろう} for the second. {山田太郎|やまだたろう} is the stock sample name on forms, like "John Smith" in English. The name itself is old-fashioned for babies today.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{桃太郎|ももたろう}→桃太郎：30946_momotarou⟧, {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}, {金太郎|きんたろう}: folk-tale heroes
- {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}になった⟦{気分|きぶん}→気分：01306_kibun⟧: feeling like Rip Van Winkle, out of touch after a long absence
